canvas-01.description: The lower half of sheet 68 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, below the title, key map and legend, is a map drawn at 120 feet to an inch of the open land in the middle of the borough between Meadow Brook and Summit Avenue. It runs from Central Avenue at the left edge east to Cedar Avenue, with Simpson Avenue entering from Summit Avenue on the west and Lake Avenue curving across the sheet from Central Avenue towards the east, where it continues on sheet 70. Laurel, Tennent and Cedar Avenues are drawn only as stubs south of Summit Avenue, which runs along the bottom edge. North of Lake Avenue the land of block 38 is divided into long numbered strips running up to Meadow Brook; south of it lie the large lots 14 to 30 of the same block. The area is almost empty: the only buildings are the Island Heights school house on Simpson Avenue near Summit Avenue, noted with stove heat and no lights, and the Island Heights pumping station, with a capacity of 140 gallons per minute and an underground gasoline tank, on a six-inch water main running north from Summit Avenue. Street widths of 50, 70 and 75 feet are given. The legend box of the atlas sits at the upper left of this half, a north arrow in block 38, and the scale bar at the bottom left.
notes: Canvas labelled 'Overview' in the manifest; printed sheet number 68.
Lake Avenue west of Laurel Avenue is Garden Avenue in OpenStreetMap; east of it Lake Avenue.
Tennent Avenue is Tennent Street in OpenStreetMap.
The key map in the upper half (sheets 68 to 74 coloured by sheet) is not georeferenced.

Printed sheet 68 (canvas label 'Overview'). Upper half is the title, key map of the whole borough (sheets 68 to 74) and legend: not placed. Lower half is a map at 120 ft to an inch of the lots between Meadow Brook and Summit Avenue (Lake Av, Simpson Av, Central Av, Summit Av; school and pumping station): one part, masked below the heavy dividing line.

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, drawn at 120 feet to an inch, covers the north-west of the borough. West End Avenue runs up the sheet along the borough line, which also follows Washington Street at the top. North of Meadow Brook lies a grid of narrow numbered lots in blocks 43 to 49, bounded by Washington Street, Jackson Street and Garden Avenue and divided by Maple, Garfield, Park and Gilford Avenues; it is almost empty, with a handful of dwellings, sheds and a green house. A few farm buildings, hen houses and a tool shop stand west of West End Avenue. Between Meadow Brook and Lake Avenue are large undivided tracts (lots 1 to 5 and blocks 38 and 39). River Avenue enters from the shore of the Toms River at the lower left, beside the railroad tracks with a coal shed and wood shed, and curves north round a small triangle to West End Avenue. Lake Avenue curves east across the lower part of the sheet; south of it the blocks 5, 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20 between West End, Chestnut, Maple, Oak, Janes, Central and Simpson Avenues are divided into narrow lots running down to Summit Avenue, with scattered dwellings and outbuildings. Street widths of 50, 60 and 70 feet are given. The scale bar sits beside the river at the lower left and a compass rose at the right edge.
notes: Jackson Street is Jackson Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Park Avenue north of Meadow Brook is Central Avenue in OpenStreetMap (its junctions with Jackson and Garden Avenues fit at 0.2 to 0.8 m).
Lake Avenue west of Simpson Avenue is Garden Avenue in OpenStreetMap; today's Lake Avenue begins further east.
Janes Avenue is Jaynes Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Borough line drawn along West End Avenue and Washington Street.
The junction of River Avenue and West End Avenue was rejected (14.6 m): River Avenue has been realigned there.

Scale 120 ft to an inch. North-west of the borough: Washington St, Jackson St, Garden Av, Maple, Garfield, Park, Gilford Avs north of Meadow Brook; River Av, West End Av, Lake Av and the lots south to Summit Av. One part.

sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, drawn at 120 feet to an inch, covers the east end of the borough, where the point between the Toms River and Barnegat Bay ends. At the top Lake Avenue crosses large undivided tracts of blocks 37 and 38, bounded on the north and east by the winding Meadow Brook, which the borough line follows. Below them Summit Avenue and Vansant Avenue cross the sheet, with blocks 31 to 34 cut into narrow numbered lots between Cedar, Beach and East End Avenues, and Bay Avenue running diagonally north-east towards the bay shore, where a yacht club house stands. South of Vansant Avenue the regular grid gives way to the curving streets of the point: Westray Avenue, Fletcher Place, Central Avenue, Ensor Place, Cedar Place, Ocean Avenue, Ocean Bend and Bayview Avenue, laid out round lettered blocks G to Q with irregular lots. The area is thinly built, with dwellings and a few outbuildings and boat houses scattered among mostly empty lots, several of them along Ocean Avenue on the river front. At the lower left Holly Avenue and the end of Lake Drive appear beside Holly Lake, which belongs to sheet 74. The Toms River lies along the south and the bay along the east. Street widths of 30, 40, 50 and 75 feet are given, and a 6-inch water pipe is marked in Ocean Avenue. The scale bar sits at the lower right and a compass rose at the right edge.
notes: Beach Avenue is Beech Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Central Avenue on the point is Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap (its junctions with Bayview Avenue, Cedar Place and East End Avenue fit at 1.6 to 2.8 m).
The junctions of Bay Avenue with Summit Avenue and of Cedar, Holly and Ocean Avenues were left out: they lay 4.4 and 4.6 m from the fit.
Borough line drawn along Meadow Brook.

Scale 120 ft to an inch. East end of the borough: Lake Av, Summit Av, Vansant Av east of Cedar Av, East End Av, Bay Av, and the curving streets of the point (Westray Av, Central Av, Fletcher Pl, Ensor Pl, Ocean Av, Ocean Bend, Cedar Pl, Bayview Av). One part.

sheet-71.description: Sheet 71 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, covers the west end of the borough where the land meets the Toms River. Along the left edge the Penn. & Long Branch R.R. runs down the shore on a causeway and trestle across the river, with the Island Heights railroad station and a freight house beside the tracks. River Avenue follows the railroad and then turns south-east along the shore, with a board walk on its water side and two small piers. East of River Avenue, Lovers' Lane curves round a fan of lots and joins a second curved lane, and a triangular park lies between the station and the lots south of Ocean Avenue. The rest of the sheet is a regular grid of narrow numbered lots in blocks 2, 6, 7, 9 and 10, bounded by Summit Avenue at the top, Ocean Avenue across the middle and West End, Chestnut and Maple Avenues running down the sheet. The blocks are thinly built, with frame dwellings, a few sheds and a hen coop. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets, and street widths of 40, 50, 75 and 90 feet are given. The lower half of the sheet is open water of the Toms River, with a compass rose and the scale bar.
notes: The Penn. & Long Branch R.R. and its trestle across the Toms River no longer exist; there is no railroad in the modern reference.
River Avenue below Ocean Avenue was drawn as a broad way between the park and the shore; its modern line differs, so its junctions with Ocean and West End Avenues were not used.
Lovers' Lane has no modern street of that name; Sassafras Lane runs nearby but was not matched to it.
Scale 60 ft to an inch. West end: River Av beside the railroad, Lovers Lane, West End Av, Chestnut Av, Maple Av between Summit Av and River Av. One part.

sheet-72.description: Sheet 72 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, covers the centre of the borough on the north shore of the Toms River. It shows four blocks between Summit Avenue at the top and River Avenue along the shore, divided by Maple, Oak, Janes, Central and Simpson Avenues running down the sheet and Ocean Avenue across the middle, with Camp Walk crossing the block between Central and Simpson Avenues and Vansant Avenue entering from the east. The northern blocks are laid out in narrow numbered lots with scattered frame dwellings. The southern blocks hold the small commercial centre: a fire station with a hose cart, a drug store, a post office and dwelling, an ice house and an ice cream parlor, stores, offices, a paint shop and a boat repair and paint shop, as well as St. Philip's Episcopal Church on Central Avenue. Two hotels stand near the river: the Perennial House between Oak and Janes Avenues and the Island House between Central and Simpson Avenues, both noted with stove heat and electric lights. River Avenue runs along the shore with a boardwalk on its water side. Below it several piers reach into the Toms River, among them the Island Heights Yacht Club house on a long pier and the Recreation Pier. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets, with street widths of 50, 70 and 75 feet. The lower part of the sheet is open water with a compass rose and the scale bar.
notes: Janes Avenue is Jaynes Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Camp Walk between Central and Simpson Avenues is West Camp Walk in OpenStreetMap.
Island Heights Yacht Club house on a pier in the Toms River.
Board walk drawn along the water side of River Avenue.
Initials and date in the lower right corner: P.H., 5/18/05.
Scale 60 ft to an inch. Centre of the borough: Maple, Oak, Janes, Central and Simpson Avs between Summit Av and River Av, Camp Walk; piers on Toms River. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-73.description: Sheet 73 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, covers the blocks between Simpson Avenue and Laurel Avenue, from Summit Avenue down to the Toms River. Vansant Avenue and Ocean Avenue cross the sheet, and Laurel Avenue jogs at Vansant Avenue, its northern stretch lying further east than its southern one. The two northern blocks, 25 and 26, are cut into many narrow numbered lots with only a few dwellings; block 25 holds the Island Heights M. E. Church at Simpson and Summit Avenues and the borough water tank (elevation 105 feet, capacity 60,000 gallons) on a six-inch main. South of Ocean Avenue lies the camp meeting ground of block 27: Camp Walk runs in from Simpson Avenue and turns north to Ocean Avenue, and Camp Meeting Avenue runs south from Ocean Avenue and then east to Highland Avenue, both lined with rows of small frame cottages on narrow lots lettered A to Q. Block A, at Highland Avenue and the curving end of Ocean Avenue, has a few more cottages, and the lower right corner shows Highland Avenue curving into Highland Bend with lots running down to the river shore. A pier reaches into the river below Camp Walk, and a boat shed stands near the shore. The blank block east of the southern stretch of Laurel Avenue belongs to sheet 74. Water pipes and hydrants are marked, and street widths of 30, 50 and 75 feet are given. A compass rose and the scale bar sit in the river at the bottom.
notes: Camp Walk is West Camp Walk in OpenStreetMap; Camp Meeting Avenue follows the line of today's East Camp Walk.
The junctions of both camp walks with Ocean Avenue were left out: the modern nodes lay 3.7 m from the fit.
Island Heights M. E. Church at Simpson and Summit Avenues; borough water tank in block 25.
River spelled Tom's River on this sheet.
Initials and date in the lower right corner: B.H., 5/18/05.
Scale 60 ft to an inch. Simpson Av to Laurel Av between Summit Av and the river: Vansant Av, Ocean Av, Camp Walk, Camp Meeting Av, Highland Av. One part.

sheet-74-1.description: Sheet 74 of the 1905 Sanborn atlas of Island Heights, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, covers the eastern part of the old camp meeting grounds between Laurel Avenue and Cedar Avenue, from Summit Avenue south towards the Toms River. Tennent Avenue crosses the northern blocks between Summit and Vansant Avenues; these blocks, 35 and 36, are cut into narrow numbered lots and hold only a stable, a wood shed and a pig sty. Block 28, between Vansant and Ocean Avenues, is laid out in large lots with a few dwellings and outbuildings, an ice house, storage sheds and a wind pump with a water tank. South of Ocean Avenue the plan changes to curving streets: Highland Avenue and Highland Bend loop round blocks B, C and D on the west, and Lake Drive runs south from Ocean Avenue and then east to Holly Avenue round block F. Cottages line both sides of Ocean Avenue, among them the Sans Souci and the Sea Breeze. The lots of block D run down to the edge of the sheet. A hexagonal inset at the bottom of the sheet, drawn separately, is not part of this map. Water pipes and hydrants are marked, and street widths of 40, 50 and 75 feet are given. A compass rose and the scale bar sit in the lower part of the sheet.
notes: Tennent Avenue is Tennent Street in OpenStreetMap.
Laurel Avenue on this sheet is its northern stretch, east of the jog at Vansant Avenue.
The south-east of the part is placed only by the junction of Lake Drive and Holly Avenue; the leave-one-out error (4.5 m) reflects that.
Cottages named Sans Souci and Sea Breeze on Ocean Avenue.

Scale 60 ft to an inch. Laurel Av to Cedar Av between Summit Av and Lake Drive (Vansant Av, Ocean Av, Highland Av, Highland Bend, Lake Drive, Holly Av), with an inset in a hexagonal frame at the bottom: the south end of Lake Drive at Holly Lake and Toms River (W. T. Rote, yacht builder). Part 2 (the inset) is not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset in a hexagonal frame: south end of Lake Drive at Holly Lake and the Toms River, W. T. Rote yacht builder (drawn out of position; no street junction (Lake Drive ends at the river); needs hand-picked control from shore or parcel corners, or carried points from sheet-70 (Holly Lake)).
